questions.q: What action does a failing liveness probe trigger?
options: The Pod is removed from the Service's Endpoints list, but the container keeps running
The kubelet kills and restarts the container
The Pod is permanently deleted and not replaced
Nothing — liveness probes are purely informational
questions.explain: A liveness probe answers whether a container should be restarted. Repeated failures cause the kubelet to kill and restart the container.

questions.q: A checkout Pod is temporarily overloaded and slow to respond, but not actually stuck. Its readiness probe starts failing. What happens?
options: The container is immediately killed and restarted
The Pod is removed from the Service's Endpoints list (stops receiving new traffic) without being restarted
The Pod is evicted from the node entirely
Nothing happens until the liveness probe also fails
questions.explain: A failing readiness probe pulls the Pod out of rotation (removed from Endpoints) without restarting it — exactly the right behavior for a temporarily overloaded, but not broken, Pod.

questions.q: Why is it a costly mistake to configure a liveness probe where a readiness probe should be used for a temporarily overloaded service?
options: It has no practical effect either way
The overloaded Pod gets killed and restarted instead of simply being paused from new traffic, making the outage worse
It causes the Pod to never receive traffic again
It automatically triggers a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scale-up
questions.explain: Using liveness instead of readiness for a transient overload condition causes Kubernetes to kill and restart a Pod that just needed a pause from traffic, compounding the problem rather than fixing it.

questions.q: What problem does a startupProbe specifically solve?
options: It replaces the need for both liveness and readiness probes
It disables liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds once, giving a slow-starting container time to initialize without being killed prematurely
It automatically scales replicas during startup
It encrypts traffic during the container's startup phase
questions.explain: A startup probe holds off liveness and readiness checks until it passes once, preventing a liveness probe from killing a container that is still legitimately finishing a slow initialization (like a large cache warm-up).

questions.q: Which probe mechanisms are available for liveness, readiness, and startup probes in Kubernetes?
options: Only httpGet is supported
httpGet, tcpSocket, and exec
Only gRPC health checks are supported
Probes can only check CPU and memory usage, not application behavior
questions.explain: All three probe types support httpGet (checking for a 2xx/3xx response), tcpSocket (checking for a successful connection), and exec (checking for a command exiting 0).
